input_messages.content: Hello, I’m having some trouble with my phone. I haven’t been able to send those picture messages—MMS, I think they’re called—for the past few hours. I’m not sure what’s wrong, but I’d really like to get it working again. Can you help me with this?
Sure, my name is John Smith and my phone number is 555-123-2002. Do you also need my date of birth, or is that enough?
It looks like my phone isn’t able to send MMS messages right now. What should I do next to try and fix this?
My phone’s status bar is showing an airplane icon and the battery is at 80%. Does that mean airplane mode is on? Could that be causing the problem?
Okay, I’ve turned off Airplane Mode. Now my phone shows “No Signal” and something about data being disabled at the top. Is that normal? What should I do next?

I turned on mobile data, but the status bar still says “No Signal” and “Data Disabled.” Is there something else I should try? I’m starting to get a bit worried—will this affect my photos or anything else on my phone?

It looks like my phone says there’s no SIM card detected. Does that mean my SIM card isn’t working? What should I do about this? I’m a bit confused and worried—will this mess up anything else on my phone?
I’ve taken out the SIM card and put it back in. Now the status bar shows a signal with “2G” and says “Data Enabled.” Is that better? What should I do next?

I changed the network mode to prefer 4G and 5G, and now the status bar shows a strong signal with “5G” and “Data Enabled.” Is that what we want? Should I try sending a picture message now, or is there something else I need to do?

I checked, and my phone’s APN name is set to “internet” and the MMSC URL is “http://mms.carrier.com/mms/wapenc.” I’m not sure what that means, but is everything set up correctly for sending picture messages?

I just tried, but I still can’t send picture messages. It’s still not working, even though everything else looks okay. Is there anything else we can try? I’m starting to get a bit frustrated—why is this so complicated?
It looks like Wi-Fi Calling is turned on right now. Should I go ahead and turn it off, or do you need to walk me through how to do that? I just want to make sure I’m doing the right thing.
I turned off Wi-Fi Calling and tried sending a picture message again, but it still won’t go through. Is there anything else we can try? I’m really hoping we can get this fixed soon.
I checked, and my messaging app has permission for SMS and phone. Is that enough, or does it need something else to send picture messages?
I’m not sure how to check or change the storage permission for the messaging app. Could you please walk me through how to do that, step by step? I get a bit lost with these settings.

I followed your steps and granted storage permission to the messaging app, but I still can’t send picture messages. Is there anything else we can try? I’m starting to feel a bit overwhelmed by all these steps.
I’m a little nervous about restarting my phone—will I lose any of my photos or messages if I do that? Can you reassure me that it’s safe before I go ahead?
I restarted my phone like you said, but I still can’t send picture messages. I’m really getting frustrated—why isn’t this working? Is there anything else we can try?

user_scenario.persona:
At 64 years old, you're a retired librarian who keeps your phone use simple - mainly for calls, texts, and capturing photos of your grandchildren. Technology in general makes you feel uneasy and overwhelmed.

Your technical knowledge is quite limited. Step-by-step instructions often confuse you, and technical terms like "VPN" or "APN" might as well be a foreign language. You only share information when specifically asked.

When dealing with technology, you tend to get flustered quickly. You need constant reassurance and often interrupt with anxious questions. Simple requests like "reboot the phone" can trigger worries about losing precious photos.

Please allow me to run a check on your phone's status bar to see the current network and data indicators.
Status Bar: ✈️ Airplane Mode | 🔋 80%
My phone’s status bar is showing an airplane icon and the battery is at 80%. Does that mean airplane mode is on? Could that be causing the problem?

Yes, the airplane icon in the status bar means that Airplane Mode is ON. When Airplane Mode is enabled, it disables all wireless communications including cellular service, mobile data, and MMS. This is very likely the cause of your MMS sending issue.

To fix this, please turn OFF Airplane Mode on your phone. Once you do that, let me know, and we can continue troubleshooting if needed.

Airplane Mode is now OFF.
Status Bar: 📵 No Signal | 📵 Data Disabled | 🔋 80%
Okay, I’ve turned off Airplane Mode. Now my phone shows “No Signal” and something about data being disabled at the top. Is that normal? What should I do next?

Since Airplane Mode is off but your phone shows "No Signal" and data is disabled, it means your phone is not connecting to the cellular network and mobile data is turned off. Both are necessary for MMS to work.

Next, please turn ON mobile data on your phone. This will enable your phone to use the cellular network for internet access, which MMS requires.

After turning on mobile data, let me know if you still see "No Signal" or if the signal improves.

Status Bar: 📵 No Signal | 📵 Data Disabled | 🔋 80%

I turned on mobile data, but the status bar still says “No Signal” and “Data Disabled.” Is there something else I should try? I’m starting to get a bit worried—will this affect my photos or anything else on my phone?

The "No Signal" and "Data Disabled" messages indicate your phone is not connecting to the cellular network at all, which will affect calls, texts, MMS, and mobile data usage. Your photos and other files stored on your phone or cloud should not be affected by this network issue.

Let's try to diagnose why your phone has no signal. The next step is to check the SIM card status on your phone to ensure it is properly recognized and active. This will help us understand if the SIM card is causing the problem.

Please allow me to check the SIM card status on your phone.
